newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX soars 2.65 pct to record close.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX soars 2.65 pct to record close.

text.p: A record run in chemicals TVK and renewed demand on the spot market after the expiry of June BUX futures pushed the BUX index to uncharted territory on Wednesday, traders said.
The BUX index surged 2.65 percent to finish at a preliminary new record of 6,480.41 points, up 167.23.

"TVK highlighted the day for all the already known reasons, but new demand after the expiry of June futures on Tuesday also contributed," one trader said. "Everybody thought the market offered new buying opportunities."

Although investors' appetite drove several stocks higher, with some of them to new record, the focus was on TVK which rallied to new records in Budapest and London, benefiting from market talks of an imminent payout by the state to the company.
TVK is expected to cash in five billion forints and an additional one billion of accumulated interest under the provisions of Hungary's previous privatisation law.

TVK surged to a new record high of 3,255 forints before closing at 3,185, up 190. In London its Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) surged to a new high of $17.75 and at 1104 GMT they were marked at $17.25.
Market participants were mixed as to what to expect for the next few days, with the trader remaining optimistic saying the futures market was also firmer, but an analyst expecting some consolidation.
"We had an above average day," the trader said. "Based on that I'm optimistic regarding the next few days, I don't think these rises would trigger profit-taking."
"Until TVK receives the six billion forints, it will rise pulling others alone," the trader added.

But an analyst said he expected a consolidation to come as approaching summer holidays might divert investors' interest from the Hungarian market which has risen more than 50 percent in forint terms since the beginning of the year.

"I think a lot of people have invested in the stocks in the year or even had positions back in 1996, have made a lot of money out of Hungary," said Nigel Rendell, emerging markets strategist at HSBC James Capel in London.
"So as far as international investors are concerned, I don't think there will be a lot of new buying," he said, adding he expected a renewed interest around autumn.
Oil firm MOL joined the record run as it hit a new high of 3,835 forints, before closing at 3,815 forints, up 85.
Pharmaceuticals Egis and meat processor Pick Szeged recovered from their losses on Tuesday which were triggered by a selling pressure due to June BUX expiry.
Egis finished at 11,900 forints and Pick at 13,600 forints, each gaining 400.
